breaking_changes: The POST /v1/images/upscale endpoint now requires the 'upscaling' model label; models without it return a 400 error — label your model 'upscaling' to use the endpoint.
OpenMOSS backend 'rocm' and 'rocm_bin' removed on Windows and Linux; use backend: vulkan or backend: cuda instead.
sd-cpp ROCm removed on Windows; users with backend: rocm will get a clear unsupported error — switch to vulkan or backend: auto.
AMD GPU entries in GET /api/v1/system-info now show a marketing name (e.g. "AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201)") instead of a raw numeric code — parse the family field for the ISA code.
Editing user_models.json no longer takes effect without a lemond restart; the restart requirement was always the implied lifecycle and is now documented.

checklist.author: @apollo-2006
checklist.text: Start the Lemonade server on a Linux machine with an AMD GPU, run curl on /api/v1/system-info, and confirm that amd_gpu entries show a human-readable marketing name (e.g. "AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201)") instead of a raw numeric version like "120001", while the family field remains the ISA code.

checklist.author: @atirna
checklist.text: Send a POST /v1/images/upscale request with a model that does not carry the 'upscaling' label and confirm the response is a 400 error with the message 'Upscale model is not labeled upscaling'.

checklist.author: @atirna
checklist.text: Send a POST /v1/images/upscale request with a model that does carry the 'upscaling' label and confirm the upscale completes successfully through the expected backend.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: Start the server with an OpenMOSS config and confirm that selecting backend "vulkan" or "cuda" works correctly, since the ROCm path no longer exists.

checklist.author: @mashan555
checklist.text: Run `lemonade launch junie --model <any-loaded-model>` on a native Windows machine (with a real or stub junie.bat) and confirm the generated `~/.junie/models/lemonade.json` contains the correct baseUrl, apiKey, and displayName fields.

checklist.author: @jeremyfowers
checklist.text: On a Windows machine, set sd-cpp backend to rocm in the config and confirm the server returns a clear unsupported-backend error rather than silently running inference at CPU speed.

checklist.author: @abn
checklist.text: Start lemond with a configured cloud provider and API key, call GET /v1/models, and confirm the discovered cloud model entry includes max_output_tokens and max_completion_tokens integer fields with non-zero values.

checklist.author: @fl0rianr
checklist.text: Run the Lemonade server artifact built from this merge on Arch Linux and confirm it starts and accepts API calls without mbedTLS linking errors.

evidence.blockers: A human with an AMD GPU on Linux must verify the new marketing-name display on /api/v1/system-info (6d0e01f). The upscaling endpoint's label enforcement and happy path need exercise (ce08204). The OpenMOSS Vulkan/CUDA fallback after ROCm removal should be tested on AMD hardware (e5d0eec). The Windows sd-cpp ROCm error path must be confirmed (d5f154a). Windows Junie profile generation needs native Windows validation (d3481a8).
evidence.breaking_changes: Five user-facing breaking changes ship: upscaling label enforcement (ce08204), OpenMOSS ROCm removal (e5d0eec), sd-cpp Windows ROCm removal (d5f154a), AMD system-info name format change (6d0e01f), and user_models.json requiring restart (1c2f67f). Each has documented migration guidance.
evidence.coverage: All 18 commits in the v2026.39.1..29b21e7 range were reviewed with CI passing. The review covers documentation fixes, model catalog additions, CI changes, dependency bumps, a structural MCP refactor, and several platform-specific backend behavior changes on AMD/ROCm.
evidence.manual_testing: AMD GPU system-info on Linux (marketing name display). Upscaling endpoint with labeled and unlabeled models. OpenMOSS with Vulkan/CUDA backend on AMD hardware. Windows sd-cpp ROCm error message. Windows Junie profile generation. Cloud provider GET /v1/models token limit discovery.
evidence.security: No security concerns observed across the release. The change set includes no new credential handling, no network calls to untrusted endpoints, no permission broadening, and no supply-chain risk beyond routine upstream dependency bumps.
